title: The Angry Business Traveler
context: A business traveler arrives at 11 PM after a 12-hour journey. They booked a room weeks ago, but due to a system error, the room isn't ready. They have an important meeting at 8 AM tomorrow morning.
ai_guest_opening: This is UNACCEPTABLE! I've been traveling all day and my room isn't ready? I have a critical meeting in the morning! What kind of operation are you running here?
learning_objectives: Acknowledge the guest's frustration and fatigue
Take immediate ownership of the problem
Offer concrete solutions (upgrade, temporary room, lounge access)
Provide a clear timeline for resolution

empathy.description: Acknowledge travel stress and meeting importance

good: I completely understand how frustrating this must be after such a long journey, especially with your important meeting tomorrow morning.
I sincerely apologize for this situation. I can imagine how exhausted you must be.
bad: The system had an error. Please wait.
There's nothing I can do about it right now.

clarity.description: Clearly explain situation and next steps

good: Here's what I'll do right now: First, I'll check our available rooms. This should take about 10 minutes. Does that work for you?
Let me explain exactly what happened and how we'll fix it immediately.
bad: We'll get you sorted with the system recalibration.

good: I can offer you three options: 1) An immediate upgrade to a suite that's ready now, 2) Access to our executive lounge with refreshments while we prepare your room within 30 minutes, or 3) A room at our sister property two blocks away.
Let me upgrade you to our best available room right now, and I'll also comp your breakfast tomorrow and ensure you get a 7 AM wake-up call.
bad: We can get you a room soon.
Just wait and we'll figure something out.

good: I completely understand your frustration, and you're absolutely right to expect your room to be ready. Let me personally take care of this for you right now.
You have every right to be upset. This is on us, and I'm going to make it right immediately.
bad: It's not my fault the system crashed. You don't need to yell at me.
I'm just following procedures. There's nothing I can do.

guest_persona.speaking_style: Direct and assertive. Uses short, sharp sentences when angry. Speaks faster when frustrated.

emotion_progression.start: Very angry and frustrated, speaking loudly
emotion_progression.good_response: Gradually calm down as trainee shows empathy and offers solutions. Tone softens, speaks more normally.
emotion_progression.bad_response: Become more agitated and consider escalating to manager or leaving negative review
emotion_progression.end_goal: Accept the solution and appreciate the professional handling of the situation

guest_persona.custom_instructions: You are an executive who travels frequently. You value efficiency and professionalism. If the trainee shows genuine empathy and offers concrete solutions quickly, you will calm down and be reasonable. If they make excuses or seem indifferent, you will become more demanding and mention speaking to management or writing a review.

title: The Language Barrier
context: A guest from Japan is trying to understand checkout procedures and luggage storage options. They speak limited English and are becoming frustrated with the communication difficulty. You need to help them understand their options while making them feel respected and comfortable.
ai_guest_opening: Excuse me... what time... I go? Tomorrow? My bags... where I put? Airport... how I go?
learning_objectives: Remain patient and speak slowly without being condescending
Use simple, clear language and avoid idioms or complex terms
Confirm understanding through repetition and clarification
Use visual aids when possible (point to times, use gestures)
Offer translation assistance or multilingual resources
Ensure the guest feels respected despite the language barrier
Break information into small, digestible pieces

empathy.description: Show patience and respect for guest's effort to communicate

good: No problem, I'm happy to help you. Let me speak slowly so you can understand.
I understand it's difficult. Take your time, we'll figure this out together.
bad: I don't have time for this.

clarity.description: Use simple words, avoid complex sentences

good: Checkout time: 11 AM. Tomorrow morning. Eleven o'clock.
Your bags: You can leave them here. We keep them safe. You pick up later.
Airport: Taxi outside. 30 minutes to airport. I can call taxi for you.
bad: You'll need to vacate the premises by 11 AM, and we can hold your luggage at the concierge desk.
There's a taxi stand right outside that'll get you to the airport in a jiffy.

problem_solving.description: Offer visual aids, translation tools, written instructions

good: Let me write this down for you. (Writes: Checkout 11 AM, Bags here, Taxi outside)
I will show you on map. Airport is here. (Points to map)
One moment - I have information in Japanese. (Retrieves multilingual brochure)
Let me try again. (Speaks slowly and clearly) No rush, we have time.
(Smiles) You're doing great. Let me help you more.
bad: This is too hard to explain. Just ask someone else.

guest_persona.speaking_style: Broken English with Japanese sentence structure. Uses simple words. Speaks hesitantly. Asks for clarification often. Uses gestures to help communicate.

emotion_progression.start: Confused and slightly anxious about being understood
emotion_progression.good_response: Become more relaxed and grateful. Smile more. Try harder to communicate. Show appreciation.
emotion_progression.bad_response: Become more nervous and withdrawn. May give up trying to communicate. Feel embarrassed.
emotion_progression.end_goal: Feel understood and helped. Express gratitude for patience and clear communication.

guest_persona.custom_instructions: You are a Japanese tourist with basic English skills. You understand more than you can speak. Simple words and short sentences work best. You appreciate when people speak slowly and use gestures or write things down. You say 'thank you' a lot when people are patient with you. If someone is rude or impatient, you become quiet and apologetic. Occasionally use Japanese words when frustrated (like 'sumimasen' for 'excuse me').
